notes: A pass means only that the tool-specific criterion was met; it is not a universal anti-bot pass.
Public tester availability, a page load, or an identifier being computed is never scored as pass.
Commercial WAF acceptance requires an owned test tenant and server-side outcome telemetry; public diagnostics cannot substitute for it.

scenarios.label: Proxied headful profile without automation attachment
scenarios.purpose: Measure the exact product profile a customer launches, before DevTools, WebDriver, or CDP attaches.

scenarios.label: Proxied headful profile through the supported automation endpoint
scenarios.purpose: Measure automation artifacts introduced by the product's documented CDP/Selenium connection path.

scenarios.label: Same profile after clean stop and relaunch
scenarios.purpose: Prove that stable surfaces and identifiers persist for one profile.

scenarios.label: Second profile with a different seed
scenarios.purpose: Prove that profile-scoped farbling and identifiers are distinct without becoming internally inconsistent.

scenarios.label: Same host without the proxy
scenarios.purpose: Prove that IP, DNS, and WebRTC tests can distinguish the host path from the protected proxy path.

scenarios.label: Stock stable Chromium on the same host and network
scenarios.purpose: Calibrate detector drift and prevent Lobium from being blamed for tester or runner-specific behavior.

tools.name: Sannysoft Antibot
tools.criterion: All scored cells are green; any allowance belongs only to the historical compatibility gate, never to release evidence.
tools.limitations: A small public JavaScript test suite. It does not measure IP reputation, behavior, TLS, HTTP/2, or commercial WAF acceptance.

tools.name: CreepJS
tools.criterion: Fingerprint data is available, totalLies is zero, and worker/iframe values agree with the main context; compare stable and distinct surfaces across scenarios.
tools.limitations: Zero lies is a fingerprint-consistency result, not a bot-management allow verdict. Only the GitHub Pages deployment is official.

tools.name: FPScanner
tools.criterion: fastBotDetection is false and every individual detection flag is false; the structured fingerprint remains coherent across the requested contexts.
tools.limitations: Client-side building blocks, not an end-to-end fraud decision. The controlled scenario may legitimately expose product automation defects that the uncontrolled scenario does not.

tools.name: Device and Browser Info bot test
tools.provider: Antoine Vastel / Device and Browser Info
tools.criterion: The returned JSON contains isBot:false and every detail flag is false.
tools.limitations: The fingerprinting test explicitly excludes IP reputation and behavior; treat it as the same provider family as FPScanner, not as an independent vote.

tools.name: FingerprintJS open source
tools.criterion: The component set is complete; the same profile is stable across relaunch; different profiles differ on intended profile-scoped surfaces. Merely obtaining a visitorId is inconclusive.
tools.limitations: FingerprintJS OSS identifies a browser and does not return a bot verdict. Its maintainers document lower accuracy than the commercial product.

tools.name: BotD
tools.criterion: A pinned self-hosted build returns a non-bot result in both Lobium scenarios and detects the deliberately automated negative control used by the lab.
tools.limitations: Same provider family as FingerprintJS. A self-hosted build must record the exact package version/commit and include a positive detection control.

tools.name: ThumbmarkJS
tools.criterion: A pinned OSS build returns complete components; the same profile is stable and different profiles are distinct on intended surfaces without cross-surface contradictions.
tools.limitations: The OSS thumbmark is an identifier, not a bot verdict. Server-side TLS, headers, IP classification, and visitorId require the separate API product.

tools.name: BrowserLeaks
tools.criterion: Proxy runs expose only the expected proxy egress; no host IP appears in WebRTC; geo/timezone/headers agree; stable and distinct rendering hashes follow the scenario contract.
tools.limitations: A suite of raw diagnostics, not a single trustworthy/untrustworthy verdict. DNS resolution still needs a system/tunnel-level control outside a browser-only proxy.

tools.name: Pixelscan
tools.criterion: No fingerprint inconsistency or automation warning; IP, DNS, location, and WebRTC sections agree with the expected proxy and negative control.
tools.limitations: Live-only and UI-driven. Preserve screenshots and raw values because labels and scoring can change without notice.

tools.name: Iphey
tools.criterion: Every section reports the expected coherent identity with no low-trust reason; record the raw section values, not only the overall badge.
tools.limitations: Opaque live scoring. A green badge is advisory and cannot replace raw surface assertions or an owned WAF result.

tools.name: AmIUnique
tools.criterion: No impossible or contradictory attributes; record rarity as a trend relative to the stock control, not as a universal threshold.
tools.limitations: Uniqueness depends on the site's changing volunteer population. The test submits fingerprint data and requires reviewer consent.

tools.name: EFF Cover Your Tracks
tools.criterion: Review detailed attributes for coherence and compare entropy to the stock control. Do not equate privacy protection or low uniqueness with commercial anti-bot acceptance.
tools.limitations: A privacy and tracker-protection research test, not an anti-bot detector. Running it contributes anonymous measurements under EFF's stated policy and requires reviewer consent.

tools.name: WebBrowserTools
tools.criterion: Normal, iframe, sandbox, eval/function, rendering, and WebRTC observations remain coherent with the profile and proxy; no host identity appears.
tools.limitations: The site's claims about aggressive extraction are not a formal guarantee. Record raw values and compare them with local probes and BrowserLeaks.

tools.name: IPLeak.net
tools.criterion: Proxy runs expose the expected egress only; WebRTC and DNS do not reveal the host ISP/location; the negative control reveals the expected different path.
tools.limitations: Browser proxies do not necessarily tunnel operating-system DNS. Interpret DNS results against the product's documented proxy model and a tunnel-level test when required.

tools.name: BrowserScan
tools.criterion: No bot flag; navigator/client-hint values agree; TLS and HTTP/2 identify the real shipped Chromium/Lobium family and do not contradict the claimed UA major.
tools.limitations: Live and opaque. Transport fingerprints should be compared with the same Lobium build and stock control, not matched to a hand-picked hash.

tools.name: Incolumitas BotOrNot
tools.criterion: The reported detection score stays in the human band and no individual test is flagged, in a headful session with real input.
tools.limitations: Includes BEHAVIOURAL tests that a scripted session cannot pass regardless of fingerprint quality, so a failing behavioural sub-score is not evidence of a fingerprint defect. Score only the fingerprint and automation sections.

tools.name: Rebrowser Bot Detector
tools.criterion: Every automation test reports green, with no CDP or isolated-world artifact detected.
tools.limitations: Targets automation plumbing rather than fingerprint values, so it is the only entry here that directly measures whether driving the browser over CDP is observable. Run it in the same mode the product actually launches profiles in — testing a hand-driven session would not measure the product.

tools.name: DeviceAndBrowserInfo bot check
tools.criterion: Classified as not-a-bot, with the device section agreeing with the persona.
tools.limitations: From the author of fp-scanner, so its heuristics overlap that entry; treat the pair as one provider family when counting independent evidence.

tools.name: WhatIsMyBrowser detection
signals: reported OS and browser version vs feature detection
tools.criterion: The parsed browser, version and OS match the persona exactly, and no "user agent looks modified" notice appears.
tools.limitations: Reads the UA and client hints and little else, so it cannot detect a deep fingerprint defect. Its value is narrow and specific: it catches a UA that disagrees with the client hints or with the engine version, which is the one lie the rest of this matrix is weakest at surfacing.
